world.bio: I captained Sydney ferries for thirty years, mostly the Manly run and the Parramatta River service. I still check the harbour from my balcony every morning with a cup of tea. My wife is recovering from a knee replacement, I play lawn bowls on Wednesdays, and the grandkids visit at Christmas. I have three shoeboxes of slides from the 1970s harbour and no projector that works.
skills_assets: Thirty years as a ferry captain, Sydney Harbour and Parramatta River
Three shoeboxes of 35mm slides from the 1970s and 80s: ferries, wharves, Circular Quay, the Harbour Bridge under repair
Detailed knowledge of harbour tides, wharves and ferry routes
A small collection of old ferry timetables and ship's logs
Member of the Sydney Ferries Retired Staff Association

projects.name: Slides of the old harbour
projects.text: I took about nine hundred slides between 1974 and 1989, mostly from the bridge of the ferry. They show old wharves, the First Fleet class ferries, and the harbour before the big towers went up. The projector died five years ago. My daughter says they can be scanned but a service quoted 2.40 dollars a slide, which is too much.

projects.name: Garden shed repair
projects.text: The roof leaks over the workbench. I patched it twice. Need a proper job but the tradesmen are booked until February.

notes.text: Out on the balcony at 6.15. A grey morning, the Manly ferry going out with the lights still on. I always say a small prayer for the skipper. Thirty years and it never gets old.

Marge did her physio today, walked the length of the hallway twice. She is cross about the stairs but the surgeon says the knee is healing well. I made her a cuppa and she smiled for the first time this week.

Looked through one of the shoeboxes this afternoon. Found a slide of the old Kuramia coming into Circular Quay, 1976. Held it up to the window light. You can just see the faces on the deck. I felt like I was back on the wheel.
Lawn bowls, lost to Barry again. He bowls like a man half his age. We had a beer afterwards and he asked about the slides. I said they are in the cupboard. He said what a waste.
Rang my son in Perth. He said he's coming at Christmas with the kids. I said bring the older one's guitar. He said it is a ukulele now. We both laughed.
Walked to the shops. Knees are all right for now. Saw a young man filming the ferries from the wharf. I wanted to tell him how the engines used to sound before the new ones, but he had earphones in.
Cleaned out the shed. Found my old captain's cap and the brass whistle. Marge says I should put them in a frame. I think I will.
Sat on the balcony with the slides spread out on the table. There are faces and places I cannot name any more. Wish I had labelled them when I could.

messages.text:
Karen: Dad, how is Mum?
Me: Walking better. Cranky about the stairs.
Karen: Don't let her do too much.
Me: She doesn't listen to me.

Barry: Beer on Wednesday?
Me: Yes, I'll beat you this time.
Barry: Dream on.
Me: We'll see.

Association: Annual lunch at the club on 15 November. Will you come?
Me: Yes, I'll bring Marge if she can manage.
Association: We'll book a table near the door.

Dan: Dad, flights are booked for 20 December.
Me: Wonderful.
Dan: Kids can't wait.
Me: Neither can I.

relations.about: Seventy, recovering from a knee replacement
Lives nearby in Balmain, visits weekly
Lives in Perth with two kids

constraints: Marge needs help at home, so he rarely goes out for more than a few hours
sensitive: Worries about memory fading as the slides lose their names
